Take this free CAT HCF and LCM online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The HCF & LCM chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT HCF & LCM tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on HCF & LCM

Finding HCF and LCM, their product relation, HCF/LCM of fractions and remainder-based word problems.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers.
  • HCF = common primes (lowest powers); LCM = all primes (highest powers).
  • HCF of fractions = HCF(numerators)/LCM(denominators).
  • Largest number dividing a,b,c with the same remainder = HCF of their differences.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Swapping the fraction rules for HCF and LCM.
  • Using HCF×LCM = product for more than two numbers (only valid for two).
  • Sign/remainder slips in "same remainder" problems.
